# SOOS — Sovereign Object (SOV)
# draft-sato-soos-sov-03
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/sov/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: September 4, 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

The Sovereign Object (SO) is the typed, stateful, policy-carrying primitive that every other SOOS governance draft assumes but none defines: the governed resource that agent authority is bound to, that Cedar policy is evaluated against, and that the audit record references. SOV defines its five-layer structure (Identity, State, Event Stream, Typed Graph, Attachment Index), its Zone A/Zone B boundary model, its five-phase lifecycle, its SO Type system, its Cedar policy context model, and the binding model by which a Mandate JWT binds an agent to a specific SO instance. Version -03 is the current version, closing out a WIMSE Security Review checklist pass against -02.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without SOV, your SOOS-governed system has no standardized way to:

- Bind agent authority to a specific, stateful, traceable resource rather than an abstract action type -- "authorized to perform action X" has no normative referent without it; any resource will do, and no audit trail is structurally required
- Guarantee that Cedar evaluation never runs against SO state or IDP intent attributes populated on the assumption of an already-validated principal/mandate relationship the pipeline hasn't actually confirmed yet -- SOV-02's evaluation order allowed exactly this, and a Stage 2 test trace confirmed the consequence directly: Cedar reached PERMIT against an MJWT with an invalid signature before a later layer caught it
- Prevent personal data from entering the kernel-authoritative audit surface -- Zone A MUST NOT contain personal data (INV-ZA-1); Zone B holds it instead, is irreversibly erasable, and is excluded from FAIP analytics by the same invariant
- Extend a governed resource type through inheritance while guaranteeing a parent type's Cedar prohibitions can never be overridden by a subtype (the SOV-02 Subtype Model)
- Make an entire operational plan itself a governed, auditable resource -- the Standing Plan Object (SPO) -- rather than leaving disaster-response or other plan-scope authority ungoverned between individual agent actions
- Satisfy GDPR Article 17 / APPI Article 19 erasure obligations while preserving the complete audit trail retention law may separately require -- Zone B Cryptographic Erasure destroys encryption keys, not records; Zone A and the Event Stream survive

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in SOV-03 and must not be paraphrased away:

Sovereign Object (SO):
   A causally ordered, policy-governed, typed, living document that evolves through a predefined finite state space under GEC authority. The unit of governance in the SOOS protocol family.

Five-layer structure:
   Identity Layer (Layer 1): so_id (UUID v7), so_type_id, human_principal_id, gec_id -- immutable identity.
   State Layer (Layer 2): current_state, current_phase, state_entered_at -- current position in the state machine.
   Event Stream: append-only, GEC-signed, causally chained via prior_event_id; soos.governance.kernel_id on every entry.
   Typed Graph: materialized view over Event Stream history.
   Attachment Index: signed references to Zone B content.

Zone A / Zone B boundary:
   Zone A is kernel-authoritative: the GEC is the sole writer; no application may write Zone A fields without a Cedar PERMIT. Zone A MUST NOT contain personal data (INV-ZA-1) -- it holds only identifiers, state references, and policy-relevant metadata. Zone B is application-managed content referenced from Zone A via a signed Attachment Index, content-hash-verified on every access. Zone B holds personal data and is irreversibly erased at Cryptographic Erasure (destroying encryption keys, not deleting records) while Zone A and the Event Stream are retained for audit -- satisfying GDPR Art. 17 / APPI Art. 19 while preserving the audit trail.

SOV-02 Subtype Model (Section 5.5, unchanged in -03):
   A registered SO Type may extend a parent type, inheriting its state machine and Cedar prohibitions while adding subtype-specific Zone A fields and transitions. A parent DENY MUST NOT be overridden by a subtype policy.

Standing Plan Object (SPO):
   soos/standing-plan-object/1.0. The only currently-registered normative SOOS subtype under the Subtype Model. A declarative operational plan as a first-class Sovereign Object: scope_constraints (geographic, SO type, agent role, temporal, delegation depth), cedar_bundle_ref (content-addressed Cedar policy bundle), cap_rrs_catalog_ref (CAP-RRS profile), idp_validation_ref (IDP structural validation schema for all plan IDPs), activation_at. Governs agents at plan scope rather than instance scope.

Mission Plan SO / Mission Status SO -- REMOVED from this document in -03:
   soos/mission-plan/1.0 and soos/mission-status/1.0 were normatively defined here in -02, duplicating subtypes AOP also normatively defines. AOP's own text states plainly these are AOP subtypes; AOP's DAG model is materially more complete (typed SEQUENTIAL/PARALLEL/CONDITIONAL dependency edges, deadline tracking, critical-path annotation, well-formedness validation) than -02's had been. -03 removes the duplicate definition entirely and defers to AOP as sole owner, including AOP's dependency-type vocabulary. Do not implement these subtypes from this document -- see draft-sato-soos-aop.

Cedar Policy Evaluation Order (Section 9.3, UPDATED in -03 -- real behavior change):
   The GEC MUST evaluate in this order:
   (1) Mandate JWT verification, full 13-step protocol (per the MJWT draft's Section 8.1). A failure at this layer is immediate DENY before any Cedar evaluation begins.
   (2) CAP Tier 0 (constitutional) prohibitions. Immediate DENY on failure.
   (3) CAP Tier 1 (jurisdictional) prohibitions.
   (4) SPO scope constraint enforcement, if the request is governed by an active SPO. Immediate DENY before Cedar evaluation on violation.
   (5) SO Type Cedar policy (parent then subtype for SOV-02 subtypes) -- with SO Instance state attributes and IDP intent attributes now populated only after MJWT verification has actually confirmed the principal/mandate relationship they assume.
   A PERMIT requires all five layers to permit. -02 placed MJWT verification LAST, as layer 5, after SO Type Cedar policy. This directly contradicted MJWT's own protocol and let Cedar evaluate -- and a Stage 2 test trace confirmed reach PERMIT -- against an MJWT with an invalid signature, before a later layer produced the correct final DENY. This is a soundness gap at the trace level, not merely a final-answer gap.

Event Stream integrity:
   Append-only, GEC-signed, prior_event_id causal chain. Entry deletion, modification, or reordering are each independently detectable: a broken prior_event_id chain MUST be reported as INTEGRITY_VIOLATION. SCITT submission (mandatory at Level 3 conformance) is performed by an independent process to prevent single-point suppression.

SO Type Registry:
   The extensible catalog of governed resource types (IANA, Specification Required). Every SO Instance is an instance of a registered SO Type, which defines the state machine, Zone A schema, Cedar policy set, and attachment types. soos/ namespace reserved for SOOS-defined types; ietf/ reserved for IETF Standards Track types.

INV-ZA-1:
   Zone A MUST NOT contain personal data. The invariant that makes the audit record itself GDPR/APPI-safe by construction rather than by redaction.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

Cedar (Amazon Web Services):
   Provides the policy evaluation semantics SOV's authorization layer depends on. SO Type declarations declare Cedar policy sets; the GEC evaluates Cedar against SO Instance state attributes exposed via the so.* context namespace -- now only after Mandate JWT verification (layer 1) has completed.

SCITT (draft-ietf-scitt-architecture):
   Provides the transparency model for SO Event Stream anchoring. Every Event Stream entry is submitted to a SCITT transparency log (mandatory at Level 3 conformance). SOV is event-centric where SCITT is artifact-centric; the SO Event Stream is the natural SCITT claim subject for governance-event transparency.

WIMSE (draft-ietf-wimse-arch):
   Establishes workload identity but does not define what workloads are authorized to act on. SOV provides that binding target: WIMSE credentials authenticate the agent; the MJWT (scoped to an SO Instance, verified before any Cedar evaluation touches it) authorizes what the authenticated agent may do to it.

DAWN (Decentralized Agent Workload Networking, BoF):
   SOV is directly relevant to DAWN's requirements in one dimension -- the governed resource agent authority is bound to. DAWN addresses agent-to-agent communication and workload routing; SOV addresses what agents operate on when they arrive at a workload. SOV's DAWN comment addresses three points: (a) the SO as the normative binding target for agent authorization in multi-workload topologies; (b) the Zone A/Zone B boundary as a portable interoperability surface -- DAWN routing can use Zone A state without touching personal data; (c) the SO Type Registry as an IANA-analogous coordination point. The SPO remains directly relevant to DAWN's orchestration requirements; only the Mission Plan SO's DAG model moved to AOP, not its relevance.

AOP (draft-sato-soos-aop):
   Sole normative owner, as of -03, of the Mission Plan SO and Mission Status SO subtypes, built on the Subtype Model SOV defines. AOP's Mission Plan SO DAG enforcement coordinates with MAD for multi-agent sub-goal assignment; HEM escalation triggered by Mission Plan SO failures is specified in AOP, not SOV.

draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-container:
   Composition, not overlap: SO governs during execution; vCon packages the resulting records for portable post-session use.

draft-ietf-oauth-resource-metadata:
   Complementary: OAuth resource metadata describes server capabilities; the SO Type Registry describes governance properties of resource types -- state machines, Cedar policy sets, lifecycle rules.

W3C PROV-DM:
   An SO's state transition sequence is a PROV-DM activity chain: each state change is an Activity, each SO state is an Entity, the GEC is the Agent.

OpenTelemetry:
   soos.so.* and soos.event.* span attributes, span naming soos.so.<event_type>, map Event Stream entries to standard trace spans. Does not substitute for SCITT submission.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

Versions below are those cited by SOV-03 as of its submission.

This draft depends on:
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-06) -- the GEC's Governance Identity Key (GIK) used to sign Event Stream entries is attested via KIA; soos.governance.kernel_id references the KIA-attested GEC identity; Event Stream integrity verification depends on KIA attestation
   Cedar -- policy evaluation semantics

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) -- the "governed object" in IDP is an SO Instance; context_refs may reference SO Event Stream entries; so.prior_denial_count composes with IDP's own prior_denial_count attribute; SPO's idp_validation_ref provides plan-specific IDP structural validation
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-06) -- HEM events bound to SO Instances; HEM_TRIGGERED/HEM_RESOLVED MUST be recorded in the SO Instance's Event Stream; HEM_PENDING prohibits all agent-initiated Transition Requests until human decision
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-07) -- GAR records generated from SO Instance Event Stream entries; Cryptographic Erasure MUST generate an ERASURE_COMPLETED GAR entry
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-05) -- CAP prohibitions enforced at the SO level, now confirmed to run only after MJWT verification (Section 9.3); SPO's cap_rrs_catalog_ref enables plan-specific CAP-RRS activation
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-05) -- binds agent authority to a specific SO Instance; so_id is the normative reference to the SO Instance Identity Layer; verified before any other Cedar evaluation layer as of -03
   MAD (draft-sato-soos-mad-04) -- cluster governance operates over shared SO instances; SPO's max_delegation_depth MUST NOT exceed the applicable MAD cluster's max_delegation_depth
   AOP (draft-sato-soos-aop-02) -- Mission Plan SO and Mission Status SO are AOP subtypes built on SOV's Subtype Model, as of -03
   FAIP (draft-sato-soos-faip-02) -- cross-domain federated analytics derived from SO Instance Event Streams; Zone B excluded from FAIP analytics by INV-ZA-1
   GRP -- the SPO is consumed by GRP for plan-scope remediation governance

---

Version history: -02 (SOV-02 Subtype Model, Standing Plan Object, Mission Plan SO / Mission Status SO subtypes, expanded Security Considerations, SO Type code namespace and SPO media type IANA registrations). -03 closes out a WIMSE Security Review checklist pass against -02: removes Mission Plan SO and Mission Status SO entirely (now AOP's sole normative subtypes, deferring to AOP's materially more complete DAG model), corrects the Cedar policy evaluation order to place Mandate JWT verification first rather than last (a confirmed real defect, not merely theoretical -- a Stage 2 test trace showed Cedar reaching PERMIT on an invalid-signature MJWT under the old ordering), and updates eight stale cross-draft version references throughout. Sections 8 through 16 renumbered down by one to close the gap left by Section 7's (Mission Plan/Status SO) removal.
